chunks: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj asked him about a man who buys food from another man who does not have it with him, and buys from him immediately. He said:

"There is no harm in it." He said: I said, "They invalidate it among us." He said: "Then what do they say regarding salam?" I said: "They see no harm in it and say: this is to a fixed term; but when it is not to a fixed term, and it is not with its owner, then it is not valid." So he said: "If there is no term, then it is more rightful for it to be allowed."

Then he said: "There is no harm in a man buying food when it is not with its owner, whether to a term or immediately without specifying a term, except when it is a sale of something whose like is not found, such as grapes, melons, and their like outside their season; then it is not proper to buy that immediately."

key_terms.أَجَلٍ: a fixed term or specified time
key_terms.السَّلَمِ: forward sale contract for delivery at a specified term
key_terms.الطَّعَامَ: food as the subject matter of sale
key_terms.الْبِطِّيخِ: melons, cited as a seasonal good
key_terms.الْعِنَبِ: grapes, cited as a seasonal good
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to buy food that the seller does not currently possess?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on buying food that is not presently in the seller’s possession. It permits such a transaction whether immediate or deferred, while making an exception for seasonal goods that are normally unavailable outside their proper time.
